prayerExcerpt.en-US: "Have a care that none lead you astray by a false philosophy," says St. Paul, for philosophy without religion is a vain thing.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: "Tomai cuidado para que ninguém vos engane com uma falsa filosofia," diz São Paulo, pois a filosofia sem religião é coisa vã.

meta.face: A Sicilian of about seventy with a sun-browned olive complexion and a SHORT, WIDE face like the busts of the old philosophers — a broad, high, DOMED forehead running into a BALD crown with a fringe of white hair over the ears, a SNUB, UPTURNED nose with a broad tip, ROUND, slightly BULGING dark eyes that twinkle under bushy white brows, broad, full cheeks, a wide mouth; a LONG, full, WAVY white beard falling to the breast; the gaze bright, humorous and kind, toward us.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. Michael Burghers's engraving (Wikipedia's lead image) shows an old man in a philosopher's cloak with a long flowing beard; Clement called him 'the Sicilian bee'. The book tells the Sicilian Stoic who became a Christian, head of the school of Alexandria before 179, missionary to the Indies who found there St. Matthew's Gospel in Hebrew left by St. Bartholomew, and died about 216. The snub-nosed, domed philosopher's head, unlike the existing St. Justin's square face, is our choice.
